subject: Bank authorization letter and remittance CSV schema for vendor onboarding
messages:
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@brightline.co>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: payments@brightline.co
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor onboarding: bank auth letter + remit CSV schema

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the quick onboarding walkthrough earlier. Attached are the bank authorization letter and a sample remittance CSV we use for AP. We want to confirm the fields you need to map into Redwood's PO/Invoice system so our finance team can send the first wire/ACH without extra back-and-forth.

Attachments: 1) bank_authorization_letter.pdf (PDF) 2) remit_csv_sample.csv (CSV) 3) W9_redacted.pdf (PDF)

Quick summary of the CSV columns we include: vendor_id, po_number, invoice_number, invoice_date, net_amount, tax_amount, remit_reference, currency, payer_account, payer_routing (we can strip payer details if Redwood prefers only remitter id + PO link).

Questions for you:
- Do you require any additional bank-letter language (e.g., explicit ACH debit authorization) for your finance team?
- What is the preferred remittance_reference format to guarantee automatic reconciliation to our invoices?
- Any lead time for the first test micro-deposit or wire?

If easier, I can hop on a 20-min call with Jordan and your payops folks.

Thanks,
Alicia Ramos
Head of Finance Ops
Brightline Logistics
(alicia.ramos@brightline.co | +1 415-555-0142)

Looping you both in — Brightline sent their bank auth letter and a sample remittance CSV. Two quick asks from finance perspective: confirm the necessary fields for automated PO-to-remit matching and whether the bank letter language is sufficient for both ACH and wire initiation.

Notes from my read: remit_reference is free-form today; they propose using "PO-{po_number}" or invoice_number. They include payer_account/payer_routing which we'd prefer not to store beyond the required compliance proof — Neha, any residency or KMS concerns there?

Alicia: we might redline the bank letter slightly (standard language for our bank team). Will confirm by 10:15.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Manager, Procurement
Redwood Inference
(marcus.lin@redwood.com)

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@brightline.co>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: bank auth letter + remit CSV schema

Thanks Marcus — quick answers inline: 
- Bank letter: we can provide an explicit ACH authorization paragraph and add language referencing "Brightline's authorized signatories". Attaching an updated PDF named bank_authorization_letter_v2.pdf. (Attachment: bank_authorization_letter_v2.pdf)
- Remit_reference: we can switch to the proposed "PO-{po_number}" format — that should be included in row-level CSV.
- Test: we can do an ACH micro-deposit and a single-wire test the week of July 14; financing prefers wire first for speed.

If Redwood requires redaction of Payer routing in your system, we can provide only a remitter_id and the full routing details in a secure doc exchange (or via SFTP).

Happy to join a call with Neha and Jordan on Thursday 10am PT.

Best,
Alicia

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@brightline.co>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: bank auth letter + remit CSV schema

Perfect — thanks Alicia and team. Quick confirmation and next steps from Redwood: 

1) Bank letter: Neha reviewed the v2 language and it's acceptable for both ACH and wire initiation provided Brightline signs with the authorized signatory listed. Neha — please confirm if you want the signed PDF stored in our vault or referenced via SFTP.

2) Remit CSV: we will map remit_reference -> PO-{po_number} and require invoice_number as secondary key. Jordan will add the CSV mapping to the vendor profile and enable automatic reconcile flagging for PO-tagged invoices. Expected mapping fields we'll persist: vendor_id, po_number, invoice_number, invoice_date, net_amount, currency, remit_reference. Payer routing/account will be kept out of the vendor profile; finance will access via secure SFTP link when needed.

3) Test move: schedule the ACH micro-deposit on July 15 and the wire test on July 16 (Brightline preferred wire-first; Redwood payops will mirror). Alicia, can you confirm routing for wire test (we will accept via secure doc or SFTP as noted)?

4) PO issuance: procurement will create the initial PO today once we get the signed bank letter in our vault. Marcus will trigger PO-100527 and loop FinOps for approval. Expect PO to appear in Brightline's remit CSV as PO-100527 in the first test file.

Action items:
- Alicia: confirm wire routing via SFTP (reply or upload to the DocuSign packet link).
- Neha: confirm vault vs SFTP preference for signed bank letter.
- Jordan: add CSV mapping and enable auto-match rule for PO-{po_number}.

If everyone is aligned I'll mark this onboarding step complete in HubSpot and set the test dates.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Manager, Procurement
Redwood Inference
(Ext: +1 206-555-0199)
